observation.visible_scene: A thin iridescent film (soap-bubble-like) stretched across a rectangular support made of two horizontal white rods (top and bottom) against a black background. The film shows a vertically stratified interference pattern: a turbulent, feathery blue/orange region at the top, followed by horizontal bands of rainbow (cyan-yellow-magenta), purple, broad green, magenta, and further green/cyan bands toward the bottom, fading to a pale grey-blue near the lower rod. A few small droplets hang beneath the bottom rod. The support frame stays fixed in the image throughout.
visible_changes: The horizontal interference color bands drift slowly and continuously downward across the excerpt (e.g., the prominent green and magenta bands sit slightly lower in later frames than in early frames), consistent with the film's pattern shifting rather than the frame moving.

The feathery/turbulent texture in the upper blue-orange zone continually reshapes: the dark blue patch at the upper left, the orange-tan streaks, and the wispy filaments change their arrangement from frame to frame.
The boundaries between color bands soften and re-form gradually; band widths and positions evolve smoothly without abrupt jumps.
The white rods, their end fittings, and the small droplets under the bottom rod remain in fixed screen positions (no camera translation or zoom is evident).
outside_clip_unknowns: How the film was created and the state before t=0 (drainage was already underway at the first frame).
Whether or when the film will thin to black or rupture after the last frame.
Any airflow, vibration, or operator action driving the upper turbulent motion.
uncertain_details: The downward drift of the bands is subtle and could partly reflect thickness evolution (colors changing in place) as well as physical translation; the excerpt cannot separate these.
The exact cause of the upper feathery motion (flow vs. evaporation pattern) is not determinable from images alone.
Camera motion is assumed absent based on the static rods, but a very slow pan cannot be fully ruled out.
